title: Reliability alignment sprint — SLO negotiation canvas and run notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working canvas for a 30–60 day cross-functional sprint to align product/feature teams, platform, and SRE on measurable SLOs, operational handoffs, and runbook commitments. It's intentionally pragmatic — workshop notes, negotiation templates, and a lightweight acceptance checklist we can use in stakeholder sessions.

Background & context:
- We have inconsistent SLO definitions across services (p95 latency vs p99 tail, different windows, different error classes).
- Several teams have requested looser latency SLOs to reduce infra cost; platform needs clearer owners for fallback policies.
- Oncall volume spikes around model rollouts and cache-warm scenarios — those need service-specific mitigations.
- Goal here is to create a repeatable negotiation/acceptance flow so SLOs become contract-like artifacts consumers and owners can reference.

Sprint goals (north stars):
1) Produce SLO negotiation packet + template for 8 target services.
2) Finalize runbook acceptance checklist and template that SRE will sign-off on.
3) Establish 2-week canary process for new SLOs with rollback criteria.
4) Record decision log and owner assignments in Confluence + link to service dashboards.

Scope (what's in/out):
- In scope: HTTP/text-generation endpoints, embedding pipelines, routing/fallback components (model-switcher), cache layer.
- Out of scope: billing/chargeback policy (will follow next quarter), long-term API contract changes.

Primary stakeholders and roles:
- Product/Feature Owner — proposes business-impact SLO (who experiences harm).
- Service Owner (team) — proposes achievable target and mitigation plan.
- Platform — provides capacity/quantization tradeoffs and fallback knobs.
- SRE — validates measurement, alerting, runbook, and accepts operational readiness.
- Solutions/SE — customer-facing constraints, security/compliance notes.

RACI (high level):
- Define SLO metric: R=Service Owner, A=Product Owner, C=Platform, I=SRE
- Measurement / alerting configs: R=SRE, A=Service Owner, C=Platform
- Runbook acceptance: R=SRE, A=SRE Lead, C=Service Owner
- Rollout policy: R=Platform, A=Product Owner, C=SRE

Negotiation template (one-pager we use during stakeholder meetings):
- Service name: (e.g., /v1/generate-text)
- Consumer(s): (internal teams, external customers)
- Business impact rationale: (what user-visible harm does failure create?)
- Proposed metric: (e.g., request_latency_ms, success_rate)
- Aggregation & percentile: (p95, p99, median)
- Target: (e.g., p95 < 250ms over 30d)
- Measurement window: (rolling 30d / 7d / 1h for alerts)
- Error class & exclusions: (e.g., exclude 503 due to deploys, or internal 4xx from canary)
- Alert thresholds: (burn rate, burst windows)
- Error budget policy: (automated throttling? release freeze?)
- Operational obligations: (oncall rotation, runbook owner, paged escalation path)
- Rollout strategy: (canary %, monitoring signals, automatic rollback conditions)
- Cost/perf tradeoffs: (acceptable increased infra cost for tighter SLO?)
- Acceptance sign-off: (SRE, Service Owner, Product Owner)

Runbook acceptance checklist (SRE gate):
- Measurement: metric instrumented and exported to telemetry (grafana/metrics link)
- Alerting: alerts present with runbook links and paging configured
- Runbook: clear step-by-step, RCA anchors, mitigations, rollback actions
- Ownership: primary + secondary oncall identified, paging escalation path validated
- Canaries: canary job created and smoke test pass criteria defined
- Handoff: link in service README and Confluence, handoff meeting recorded

Two-week canary process (proposed):
Week 0: negotiate template, SRE validates metric instrumentation, staging canary run.
Week 1: 5% traffic canary for 48–72hrs, monitor burn-rate and latency histograms.
Week 2: 25% for 72hrs, check error budget and customer-facing metrics; if stable proceed to full rollout.
Rollback triggers (examples):
- sustained burn rate > 4x for 60m OR
- p99 latency regression > 2x baseline for 30m OR
- customer-visible errors increase by > 3x in a 1h window

Workshop agenda (90m) — session template we can reuse:
- 0–10m: context and goals (Product + SRE lead)
- 10–25m: Service owner presents proposed metric/target + data snapshot
- 25–45m: Platform chunk — capacity/knobs and suggested quant profiles
- 45–70m: Live negotiation using the template — fill fields, call out exclusions
- 70–85m: Acceptance criteria & runbook checklist review
- 85–90m: Assign next actions and signatory owners

Communication plan:
- Post-workshop: update Confluence decision page and attach packet within 24h.
- Announce in #reliability with the short decision digest and oncall implications.
- Tag affected teams and schedule 30-min ops handoff within 72h.

Risk register (quick):
- Risk: measuring different percentiles yields incompatible alerts. Mitigation: standardize on a platform-level config mapping (p95 for user latency, p99 for tail-critical services).
- Risk: teams underreport mitigations => more pages. Mitigation: require a mitigation runbook entry before sign-off.
- Risk: model rollouts introduce repeated transient errors. Mitigation: enforce model-canary cadence + traffic shaping.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Do we require a unified telemetry field name or allow service-specific metric names? (platform prefers unified names for ownership)
- Who owns the policy that converts error budget burn into automated throttles? (platform or product?)
- Need legal review for external SLAs if we expose a customer-facing SLO.
- Build a small dashboard template for negotiation sessions (perf distro + error budget timeline).

Deliverables by sprint end:
- 8 completed negotiation packets + signed acceptance rows in Confluence
- Runbook checklist template committed to repo and used for at least 4 services
- A lightweight canary job template in infra repo (example: k8s job + smoke test)
- Decision log captured (who signed what and why)

Action items (initial):
- [Jonah] create Confluence decision page and copy this canvas — due 2026-10-14
- [Asha] prototype canary job template in infra repo and open PR — due 2026-10-21
- [Service Owners] fill negotiation template for target services and attach histograms — due 2026-10-19
- [SRE] schedule workshop slots; prioritize teams with highest customer impact — due 2026-10-16

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working document; expect edits and tighter language after the first two workshops.
- The goal is not perfect SLOs on day 0 but a reproducible negotiation flow and clear ownership.

Appendix (links & small snippets):
- Example SLO snippet (yaml):
  metric: http_request_latency_ms
  aggregation: p95
  target: 250
  window: 30d
  alert: burn_rate > 2 over 1h

- Quick glossary:
  Error budget = 1 - SLO over measurement window;
  Burn rate alert = speed at which budget is being consumed;
  Canary = partial traffic rollout to validate assumptions.

End of canvas — notes and edits welcome.
